severity_native: HIGH derived (SG-1; MEDIUM native) / BLOCKING (architect ARCH-1) / CRITICAL derived (unhappy-path UP-1)
trigger: a confined caller whose VisibleSet exceeds kScopePushdownMaxIds (10000) pages GET /api/v1/inventory/software or MCP query_installed_software with a small limit; a full scanned window whose LAST row belongs to an out-of-scope device
classification_rationale: read_devices_page encodes next_cursor from rows->back() BEFORE the post-filter (:901-903); the d1 cursor is plain base64url of name 0x1F agent_id 0x1F install_id (round-tripped by two reviewers); the unit test test_software_catalogue_model.cpp:355-362 pins the leak by asserting the decoded cursor carries the dropped agent 'b'; docs call the cursor opaque and say devices_omitted is the only signal
summary: Out-of-scope agent_id, software name and install_id are returned to a confined caller on every wide-scope page, so with limit=1 the caller can enumerate out-of-scope devices: a confinement escape stronger than K2's existence count. Derived I1 (HIGH) raised by E2 (a confined operator reading beyond confinement) to CRITICAL; E4 (scope above 10000) is no downgrade. Independently found by security-guardian, architect and unhappy-path (same wave, none shown the finding). Fix: build the cursor from the last IN-SCOPE row (bounded server-side refill) or seal the token; invert the test at :355-362; mutation: restore rows->back() pre-filter and the test must fail. Fold UP-3 (cursor separator) into the same codec change.

severity_native: HIGH derived (UP-2) / LOW (happy-path HP-1, which saw only the name:123 and string-limit triggers)
trigger: MCP query_installed_software called with a wrong-typed known argument: version 2.0 (float), array, null or bool is dropped so the query runs UNFILTERED across the fleet; limit 18446744073709551615 wraps to -1 and clamps to 1 row; agent_id/name 123 is stringified and filters to '123' returning an empty 200
classification_rationale: catalogue_params (mcp_server.cpp:267-279) leaves non-string/non-integer values out and query_installed_software never calls strict_args_error (:8959-8960); the response does not echo the applied filters, so a caller cannot tell the filter was dropped; the repo's own #2970B standard treats a silent default substitution for a wrong-typed argument as a defect
summary: The new `version` filter on this tool can be silently ignored, returning every row where the caller asked for one version, and the result reads as correct (I3). Name/agent_id/limit leniency is pre-existing and documented as 'ignored like the other read tools'; the new filter makes it a wrong-result hazard. Design decision (e) covers unknown ARGUMENT NAMES, not wrong types on known arguments. Fix: a type-only check for agent_id/name/version/limit/cursor on query_installed_software returning kInvalidParams (reuse strict_args_error's type arm), stringify only limit; test: version 2.0 and limit as string return -32602; mutation: remove the check and the test fails. Alex may instead accept the pre-existing lenient convention for name/agent_id, but version must be strict.

trigger: an agent_id that contains 0x1F: decode_devices_cursor peels the two trailing fields with rfind so the separator inside the agent_id splits the wrong field, the decoded keyset position becomes (name+0x1F+prefix, suffix, id), and the walk skips every remaining same-name row that sorts before it
classification_rationale: Register gates agent_id by length only (agent_service_impl.cpp:103); the enrollment chokepoint auth_db.cpp agent_id_ok rejects bytes <= 0x1F so an agent enrolled normally cannot carry one, but whether every Register path (non-default/no-enrollment modes) is covered is not proven; a silent page-walk skip is a wrong-result-as-correct (I3)
summary: Exposure is narrowed by the enrollment chokepoint but not proven closed, so it gates (E4/E5 are no downgrade). It is folded into the same codec change as the cursor-disclosure finding: encode each field separately (base64 per field) or reject 0x1F in the keyset key, and add a round-trip test with a 0x1F agent_id.

trigger: no-name/no-agent_id query with version= (REST and MCP) or kind/ecosystem/source (REST) on a fleet of ~10^8 installed_software rows; only (name,agent_id,install_id) and (agent_id) indexes exist, so these filters scan; only the q arm goes through bounded_query (5 s)
classification_rationale: software_inventory_store.cpp:959-984,1032-1040: the other filters take a plain try_acquire_for lease capped only by the pool's 30 s statement_timeout on the shared 16-connection pg_pool_; ingest acquires with a 500 ms timeout
summary: About 16 concurrent unanchored callers can starve ingest and other reads; bounded at 30 s per request so not HIGH. The store code is unchanged; this PR adds the callers (version on both transports, the REST filters). Separate store surface: deferred to an issue (draft 01); relates to #5661 and #5662.
